plugins.name: no-cape
plugins.description: Lean engineering-discipline skills for frontier-class models — plus a cape mode that enforces the same discipline on the model tiers that still need one.

skills.name: clarifying-requirements
skills.description: Use when starting a new feature, component, or project whose requirements are underspecified or ambiguous — before designing or writing code
headings: First: has the approach been chosen?

skills.name: durable-plans
skills.description: Use when planned work will outlive the current session — persisting a plan to disk, resuming work from an on-disk plan, or landing changes a plan file describes
headings: When to persist — and when not to

skills.name: escalate-dont-thrash
skills.description: Use when repeated attempts at the same problem keep failing without producing new evidence — before trying another variation of the last fix
headings: Why this is a win, not a defeat

skills.name: exploring-approaches
skills.description: Use when starting a new project or significant feature from a vague idea — before clarifying details or planning, especially when the user already has a preferred approach
headings: The brake: when to speak, when to move on

skills.name: fail-loud
skills.description: Use when writing error handling — try/catch blocks, fallback values, default parameters, retries, or any code path that handles failure

skills.name: measure-before-optimizing
skills.description: Use when asked to improve performance, or when about to optimize code believed to be slow

skills.name: receiving-feedback
skills.description: Use when receiving code review comments, reviewer suggestions, or technical corrections — before implementing any of them

skills.name: root-cause-debugging
skills.description: Use when encountering a bug, test failure, regression, flaky test, or unexpected behavior — before proposing or applying any fix
headings: Multi-component systems (API → service → DB, CI → build → deploy)

skills.name: safe-refactoring
skills.description: Use when restructuring, renaming, moving, or extracting code that already works — before making the first edit

skills.name: schema-migration-safety
skills.description: Use when writing database schema migrations or changing tables, columns, indexes, or constraints on a system with real data

skills.name: surgical-changes
skills.description: Use when editing existing code — bug fixes, small features, or any change inside a codebase you didn't just write
headings: When you see something worth improving

skills.name: verify-before-done
skills.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing — before committing, opening a PR, marking a task done, or relaying a subagent's success report
headings: Check the criterion, not just the run

skills.name: writing-meaningful-tests
skills.description: Use when writing or modifying tests, adding mocks, or tempted to add test-only methods to production code

skills.name: writing-solid-plans
skills.description: Use when designing or planning a multi-step feature, refactor, or spec before implementation begins
headings: If the plan outlives this session

commands.name: no-cape
commands.description: Manually load a no-cape discipline skill and apply it to the current work
